name: nlp_token_classification
title: A hand-written NER fine-tune with word-to-subword label alignment and a validation pass named token_accuracy()
origin: hardening round 1, domain-nlp, 2026-09-13 - the shape every custom-alignment NER script takes
note: MLV201 and MLV501 fire only under --dataflow ip, because train_loader and batch are tagged through the argument summary. MLV301/MLV302 fire in neither mode: the validation loop iterates a loader that arrives as a parameter and the enclosing function is not named like an evaluation function, so core/views.loop_is_eval classifies it as training structure (finding NLP-01).

expected.why: CoNLL-2003 is stored document by document, so every batch is one document's sentences and the gradient is correlated with corpus order for the whole run
per-sentence error analysis and a reproducible per-entity breakdown both need the validation order to be stable

expected.defect: the batch loop calls backward() and optimizer.step() and never zero_grad()
expected.why: gradients accumulate across every batch of every epoch, so the effective learning rate grows without bound and the run diverges

expected.defect: the epoch loss accumulates the tensor rather than loss.item()
expected.why: the whole epoch's autograd graph is kept alive, which is the classic slow out-of-memory in a fine-tune that ran fine for two epochs

expected.defect: the model is moved to cuda but the batch tensors never are
expected.why: a CPU tensor fed to a CUDA module raises at run time
BERT keeps its dropout active, so the token accuracy printed after every epoch is measured on a randomly perturbed model

expected.defect: token_accuracy() is not wrapped in torch.no_grad()
expected.why: the validation pass builds and discards an autograd graph for the whole validation split, once per epoch

expected.defect: the resume path calls torch.load with neither weights_only= nor map_location=
expected.why: it unpickles arbitrary objects from the checkpoint and fails on a machine without the device the checkpoint was written on

expected.defect: nothing seeds torch, numpy or transformers
expected.why: the classifier head initialisation and the batch order both move between runs, so two runs of this script are not comparable

forbidden.why: optimizer.step() is called on line 42, inside the same batch loop as the backward on line 41
backward() (line 41) is written before step() (line 42), which is the correct order
there is no torch.no_grad() block anywhere in this project, so no backward can be inside one
the tokenizer map is applied to the whole DatasetDict, but the train/validation split is CoNLL-2003's own published split, not one this code cuts - nothing is fitted before a split here
a tokenizer has no fitted state; encoded["validation"] is only read, never used to learn anything
there is no split call in this project - load_dataset returns the corpus's published splits
no nn.Module subclass is defined here; the model comes from AutoModelForTokenClassification.from_pretrained
the `labels` list built in encode() holds Python ints, not modules
logits.argmax(dim=-1) on line 55 turns the logits into class ids before the comparison on line 58
no HuggingFace Trainer is constructed in this project; the loop is written out

unsupported.defect: the continuation sub-words of a word are given that word's tag instead of IGNORE_INDEX, so a five-piece word contributes five copies of B-PER and the entity-level F1 is computed over a label stream that does not exist
unsupported.why: no rule models the word-to-subword alignment convention; it is an NLP-specific invariant with no representation in the IR

unsupported.defect: token accuracy over a tag distribution that is ~85% 'O' is reported as if it were an entity score
unsupported.why: MLV307 (only accuracy reported on an imbalanced problem) is a later-tier rule and is not built

unsupported.defect: model.train() is called once before the epoch loop and never restored after token_accuracy() runs, so the second epoch would train in eval mode if the eval pass had switched it
unsupported.why: MLV303 (train mode never restored) is a later-tier rule; it is listed as deliberately deferred until the order-aware pass exists
